questions.text: Consider a B+ tree index to be built on the attribute EmployeeID of a table Employees , with the following properties: • The length of the attribute EmployeeID is 16 bytes. • The size of each child pointer is 8 bytes. • The size of each disk block size is 512 bytes. • The size of each record pointer is 10 bytes. With the given information, what is the best choice for the order of the non-leaf nodes of the B+ tree?

options: {A → D, C → D, AB → C, D → A}
{C → D, AD → B, AB → D, D → C}
{A → B, C → D, AB → C, D → B}
{C → D, AB → D, B → A, A → D }
questions.correct_answer: {C → D, AB → D, B → A, A → D }

questions.text: Consider a relation schema S (A,B,C,D,E,G) and the set of functional dependencies, F = {A → BC, B → D, D → E, E → B, C → G}. This schema is decomposed into two relations S1 (A,B,D,E) and S2 (A,C,G). Consider the following statements given below regarding the decomposition of S1 and S2 . Choose the correct option(s).
options: The decomposition of S into S1 and S2 is dependency preserving.
The decomposition of S into S1 and S2 is lossless.
The schema S1 is in 2NF.
The schema S2 is in 3NF.
correct_answer: The decomposition of S into S1 and S2 is dependency preserving.
The decomposition of S into S1 and S2 is lossless.

questions.text: [IMAGE: /data/images/cs2001_2026T1_ET_FN_p9_Im4.webp|block] Which of the following sequences will result in the given tree?

options: RAID 0 only uses data striping, no redundant information is maintained.
RAID 1 employs mirroring, maintaining two identical copies of the data on two different disks.
RAID 3 consists of bit-level striping with dedicated parity.
RAID 4 write performance is high as parity is distributed over multiple disks.
correct_answer: RAID 0 only uses data striping, no redundant information is maintained.
RAID 1 employs mirroring, maintaining two identical copies of the data on two different disks.
